speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text: The swelling on the nape of the neck that is painless and progressive, combined with your history of colon cancer, raises concern for a metastatic lesion or a specific soft tissue tumor. I need to visualize the internal structure to distinguish between a lipoma, cyst, or solid mass. REQUEST TEST: MRI of the neck and soft tissues.

speaker: Patient
text: Overall healthy appearance, no other complaints or symptoms noted. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pneumonia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: The previous doctor's suggestion of pneumonia is clinically inconsistent with a painless, progressive neck mass on the nape, so I will disregard that assessment. I am proceeding with the MRI of the neck to characterize the mass given your history of colon cancer. REQUEST TEST: MRI of the neck and soft tissues.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: The MRI of the neck and soft tissues reveals a well-defined, encapsulated mass located in the subcutaneous tissue of the nape of the neck, measuring approximately 2.5 cm. The lesion demonstrates signal characteristics consistent with mature adipose tissue (lipoma) on T1 and T2-weighted images, with no evidence of internal vascularity, invasion into surrounding structures, or lymphadenopathy. There is no indication of metastatic disease from the prior colon cancer in this region.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the clear MRI results, which confirm this is a benign lipoma and rule out metastatic disease. Since it is asymptomatic and not causing any functional issues, I recommend we simply monitor it for any changes in size or consistency.
